html:
The Q'eqchi' are a Maya people of the highlands of Alta Verapaz in Guatemala, and today also of the lowlands of Petén, southern Belize and southern Mexico. Their language, Q'eqchi', has close to a million speakers.

Before the Spanish came their towns lay in the mountains of Alta and Baja Verapaz. They and their neighbours fought off Spanish armies so well that the region was called Tezulutlán, "land of war". In the 1530s and 1540s Dominican friars led by Bartolomé de las Casas won it over by peaceful preaching, and it was renamed Verapaz, "true peace". In the late 1800s German coffee planters took much of their land, pushing many Q'eqchi' north and east into new forest land. Their neighbours include the Poqomchi'. See Guatemala and Maya city-states.
